title: Whole Castellated Web and Continuous Flange Beam
description: One newly authored complete castellated I-section architectural beam. Two broad uninterrupted full-length flanges are welded continuously into one deep central web, whose five complete hexagonal through apertures have real finite reveals and retained solid end posts. The whole long lower flange is the ground datum; the entire section and both complete I-shaped end faces are supplied, not a cropped render or separated beam fragments. All web, reveal and flange triangles share one closed connected material boundary without overlapping internal plate faces. Unlike the solid uninterrupted web of the earlier workshop jib beam, this independent whole member has actual bounded through-web cavities and full-depth intermediate posts; no column, trolley, hook or old beam mesh is imported or extracted. Three opaque constant untextured PBR roles, metres Z up, full horizontal envelope centred at the lower flange sole. One original architectural module zero scenes. Fixed castellated-beam-inspired art only: invented proportions and openings are not a fabricated section specification or construction detail. No welding procedure, service routing, joint fit, structural analysis, deflection, stability, span rating, load capacity, fire performance, manufacture, installation or building safety capability made or verified. No rigging, animation or interaction.
